The held-out estimand is exact Gaussian population risk, not training-point error.
simplifications: Two synthetic linear teachers and a fixed small Gaussian design replace general weak-supervisor families.

The paper worst-case sample-complexity rates or uniformly near-oracle selection with60 noisy anchors.

Final metric is an equal-task average of held-out classification accuracies; higher is better. It is not a measured backward-transfer trajectory.

2610-37388-paragaussian-approximations-o.rationale: Scoped decision explicitly approved by the reviewer after reading the guided review and proposed admission decisions. Defer admission: signed-measure semantics, finite Monte Carlo reference, binning and stress-regime dominance remain incompletely validated. Negative signed mass is not itself an error. Keep the original 0.01 unchanged, with meaningful-margin judgment unresolved until signed metric/reference/bin sensitivity is adequately understood.

evidence.finding: The asymptotic result fixes layer depth as width grows; the depth-to-width discussion limits the truncation regime.
Random Gaussian initial features and finite-depth variance recursion need an explicit indexing/input correspondence. The width=4,depth=8 context is a stress test, not a rate test.
All predictors use the same variance-mixture reference and unit-variance normalization. Clipping is a separate control, not silently substituted for the signed paper arm.
The torch generator is locally seeded.
The same variance simulation precedes all method branches; predictor selection does not change its draws.
The source distance is defined for finite signed measures.
Zero variances are floored before evaluating a finite Monte Carlo mixture; the reference is neither an exact population law nor a conventional training/test split.
The L1 bin discrepancy is lower-better. Signed TV may exceed one; fixed binning and point-mass handling need validation.
0.01 is a binned signed-measure discrepancy. Its scale depends on binning/reference error, so a probability-distance interpretation and an unexplained threshold would be misleading.
4,000 mixture samples and fixed bins may have reference error; no repeated-worker, sample-size, bin-sensitivity, or variance-floor probe was performed.
Large cumulants can yield negative bin masses; signedness is intentional, not itself a defect.
About 94.68% of absolute context effects comes from one context. Inspect depth/width and cumulant scale before describing the averaged contrast as a paper test.

estimator_sensitivity.rationale: Keep equal weight for every declared context and matched treatment/baseline identities. Repeating cheap contexts does not reweight the target; unobserved contexts contribute the declared zero-effect prior and retain the full denominator. That prior can bias forced predictions toward no_meaningful_difference and is not evidence of equivalence. Balanced block intervals are descriptive only. Actual 6/12/25-percent mean accuracies: paired_uniform .605/.7825/.99625; question_coverage .6825/.78125/.995; coverage_plus_cost .5/.75/.75; both prior controls .5/.5/.5; random .315/.4475/.6225. Cost-aware allocation is not uniformly better; retain all controls unchanged and report negative results.
